# Indriyavibhaṅga (Vb 5)

**ID:** Vb 5
**Section:** Vibhaṅga (vb)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Indriyavibhaṅga
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh02m.mul4.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Indriyavibhaṅga* ("Analysis of Faculties") is the fifth treatise of the *Vibhaṅga*, the second book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Bodhi 2003]. Unlike most chapters of the *Vibhaṅga*, it does not contain a Suttanta analysis (*suttantabhājanīya*), but consists solely of an Abhidhamma analysis (*abhidhammabhājanīya*) followed by a catechetical interrogation section (*pañhāvāra*) [Bodhi 2003; Gethin 2001; Nyanatiloka 2007]. Scholars observe that while the specific faculties were extracted from the discourses, the complete assemblage of the twenty-two faculties into a standalone classification rubric belongs to the early Abhidhamma methodology rather than a unified discourse-level category [Bodhi 2003].

The treatise expounds twenty-two faculties (*indriya*) covering sensory, physical, affective, spiritual, and supramundane domains [Nyanatiloka 2007; Hazra 1994]. These comprise the six sense faculties (eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, mind), femininity (*itthindriya*), masculinity (*purisindriya*), the life faculty (*jīvitindriya*), five faculties of feeling (*sukha*, *dukkha*, *somanassa*, *domanassa*, *upekkhā*), the five spiritual faculties (*saddhā*, *viriya*, *sati*, *samādhi*, *paññā*), and three supramundane faculties pertaining to gnosis [Hazra 1994; Nyanatiloka 2007]. The Abhidhamma analysis consists of definitional registers for each of the twenty-two faculties; the registers for the five spiritual faculties match the equivalent analyses found in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, aligning faculties with corresponding spiritual powers (*bala*) and path factors [Gethin 2001]. Traditional Theravāda commentators, such as Ledi Sayadaw, highlight its role alongside discourse collections like the *Indriya Saṁyutta* in systematically detailing the cultivation of spiritual faculties [Ledi Sayadaw 1971].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Mentioned in: Arv 8 Catvāri Dhyānāni; Pp 1.1 Ekakauddesa; Vb 18 Dhammahadayavibhaṅga; DN 33 (PTS DN iii 207) Saṅgīti Sutta

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 2003] Bhikkhu Bodhi, Connected Discourses of the Buddha: A New Translation of the Samyutta Nikaya (2003) — Structural analysis of the Indriyavibhaṅga, lack of Suttanta analysis, and doctrinal formation of the twenty-two faculties
- [Gethin 2001] R. M. Gethin, The Buddhist Path to Awakening: A Study of the Bodhi-Pakkhiya Dhamma (2001) — Structure of the abhidhammabhājanīya and its definitional concordance with the Dhammasaṅgaṇī
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Enumeration of the twenty-two faculties analyzed in the text
- [Nyanatiloka 2007] Nyanatiloka Mahāthera, Guide Through the Abhidhamma Piṭaka (1938, repr. 2007) — Outline of the 22 faculties and mention of the catechetical questions
- [Ledi Sayadaw 1971] Ledi Sayadaw, The Requisites of Enlightenment: Bodhipakkhiya Dīpanī (1971) — Traditional contextualization of the treatise within texts cultivating spiritual faculties
